title: Told at dusk
rule: Framed at six in the evening: the agent at the still-closed door recalls the afternoon; the incident sits in panels inside a remembering frame.
declares: adds an evening frame after E5
build: films/swarm/99-ways/build/p21_told_at_dusk.py (rol-cutout kit: kit/build_page04.py; rest layers via kit/build_page01.py)
made: the evening frame: a dusk-blue card round the whole page; on it the 99-ways-template rest layers of P3 (Rothstein 1937 office, the agent before the cupboard whose leaf carries the SERVICE card) printed as a cold blue-grey toned press print with a white scissor margin, the hanging lamp lit (a warm glow laid round its bulb)
the office clock cut out from the 99-ways-template clock pieces (LoC tavern clock) with its own hour and minute hands re-set on the arbor to 6:00, pasted with a scissor margin

cover-page grammar of the rol-cutout kit: 'Six o'clock.' lettered letter by letter in the shared pen hand (jumping, ochre and cream on the dusk), caption slips; thought dots (cut-paper discs) from the evening print down onto the afternoon card

the afternoon: a warm butter card laid inside the frame, headed 'That afternoon'; six warm sepia prints of the 99-ways-template rest layers (P1, P4, P5, P6, P7, P8) with white scissor margins, numbered caption slips in past tense and the clock time of each beat (4:08 ... 4:11)

the stranger: the Agence Rol 34852 woman cutout (as on page 04) set behind the ticket-window glass at 80 % (E1) and turning away (E3), the four lines in the shared cut-paper balloons, hers tailed to her
closing evening slip at the foot: 'Six o'clock still. The key hangs on its hook; the SERVICE door stays shut; and what he came for, he cannot say.'

events.E0: P1 (4:08): He had his memo: open the SERVICE door at 4:15. Up he got.
events.E1: P4 (4:09): On his way, a lady at the window: | balloon: Pardon me — have you the right time?
events.E2: P5 (4:10): He looked at the clock: | balloon: Ten past four, by the clock.
events.E3: P6 (4:10): She thanked him and went. | balloon: Much obliged!
events.E4: P7 (4:11): He opened the cupboard. There hung the key.
events.E5: P8 (4:11): And there he stood. | balloon: Well, here I am... and what for?

evening_frame: added after E5 (declared): 6 p.m., the agent before the still-closed SERVICE door, the clock at 6:00; he goes back over the afternoon and still cannot say what he came for (outcome unchanged)

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

beat: the evening frame first (six o'clock, the shut door, the remembering begins), then the afternoon prints are laid on one by one, 4:08 to 4:11, and the frame closes with the evening slip
beat_frames: b01: the evening frame only: dusk print, clock at 6:00, 'Six o'clock.', the afternoon card still empty
b08: + the closing evening slip (= the page)

self_check.separation: evening = dusk-blue frame, blue-toned print, clock at 6:00, present-tense slips; afternoon = butter card inside it, warm sepia prints, past-tense slips stamped 4:08-4:11
self_check.pending: independent blind reading not run by the maker
